review_highlights.comment: Dr. Fisher is pretty much a campus legend.

Probably the best professor I have ever had. Seriously. No one has made science as interesting and easy to understand for me than Dr. Fisher. He preaches science literacy, which is an issue for many students. If science is not your best subject like it was for me, Fisher can definitely change that. Awesome dude, highly recommend.

Take his lower division ASTR classes. You will never look at the world again. You will look up at the night sky in awe, you will begin to understand life beyond the biological level, but the astronomical level. His lectures are some of the most inspiring I've attended, and my mind was blown and had goosebumps of astonishment on a weekly basis.

Dr. Fisher is the man! He isn't really focused on teaching you astronomy, as he is on getting you stoked about astronomy. Most of his lectures are him showing you really cool space related photos, and then explaining the science behind it. The tests are slightly harder than you'd expect but not bad at all. He just really wants to make the class fun

Fisher is INCREDIBLE. Im a junior this year and have taken so many different classes but if you were to take one class at UO, it would be ASTR 121/122 with Dr. Fisher. You learn about the grand scale of the world you live in. You ever watch a Neil deGrasse Tyson video, and you get goosebumps from the shear astonishment? Yeah, this class does that!

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed this course and Dr. Sterner. The exams were very reasonable if you went to lecture/discussion sections (especially before exam days--like flat out would tell us some of the questions). When I had a family emergency at the beginning of the term she was very empathetic and offered to let me reschedule our midterm no questions asked.

I loved Kirsten. Her class was a great mix of anthro and practical application with a lot of fun medical/bio stuff included as well. There was a textbook assigned but you dont need to read that so much as the novel she assigns for 376. It was a fantastic read and was more interesting than any text book. I would love to take another class from her.

This hybrid class was interesting and fun. Sterner's lectures were comprehensible and well rounded. The labs were helpful and definitely a key to success. She was lenient and understanding, when appropriate but held her ground. Lectures could feel never ending sometimes but were interesting and important for tests in the long run.

I really enjoyed this class. Her exams are very lecture based, and the readings she requires every lecture WILL show up on the exams (but will be straight forward). The lectures are very interesting and I found her to be a very engaging lecturer. There are weekly pre-discussions assignments and 5 or 6 annotation assignments that are pretty short.

Did not have experience with genomics other than some base level stuff from hs. Didn't find this class that difficult, 3 exams and 2 essays is rly all you have to do and the essays are straight forward. Spend more time studying for exam 2 and you'll be good. Final might be hard but idk cause it got switched to online due to the virus. Good luck!

Greg is an awesome educator and yes, even lets you call him Greg. I've only had him two weeks so far but he's great. Only four actual homework assignments in the term but they're (slightly) harshly graded. :)
